root.name: Bishop's Opening: Lisitsyn Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Bc4 c6 3. d4 d5 4. exd5 cxd5 5. Bb5+ Bd7 6. Bxd7+ Nxd7 7. dxe5 Nxe5 8. Ne2

overview: The Philidor Counterattack leads to open exchanges: after 5.Bb5+ Bd7 6.Bxd7+ Nxd7 7.dxe5 Nxe5 8.Ne2 Black has an isolated d5 pawn but active pieces and open lines. Black plays ...Nf6 and ...Bd6 or ...Qb6 with active pieces; White completes development with Nbc3 and O-O. Level play with simple plans.

white_ideas.idea: Develop Nbc3 and castle, then attack the d5 pawn with Nf4 or Nbc3.
Exploit the half-open d-file against Black's isolated d5 pawn.

black_ideas.idea: Develop quickly with ...Nf6, ...Bd6, ...O-O; use the knight on e5.
Push ...d4 if the knight on c3 can be driven away.

typical_structures.structure: Black isolated pawn on d5 against White's lack of a d- and e-pawn; open e-file.

character.notes: Simple development with a mildly weak d5 pawn for Black and open lines but nothing forcing.

soundness.notes: Reasonable equal position for both sides.

structure.notes: Exchange structure with the e-file open and an isolated d5 pawn.

approach.notes: A respectable line of the Bishop's Opening, not rare at the top level.

level.notes: Clear plans around the isolated pawn, little to memorise but not a first-repertoire line.
